subject.title: Externally-registered cron jobs auto-enable without user confirmation, inherit expensive default model, no usage circuit breaker

question: What default policy should OpenClaw apply to externally or plugin-registered recurring agent-turn cron jobs that can spend model quota?
rationale: The source-reproduced behavior is real, but the fix changes compatibility-sensitive cron defaults, plugin scheduling contracts, provider/model spend policy, doctor/update behavior, and security provenance.

options.title: Default Disabled With Diff
options.body: Externally or plugin-registered recurring agent-turn jobs start disabled until an operator reviews a doctor/update diff and enables them, with explicit model or safe model policy required.

options.title: Keep Enabled With Strong Guards
options.body: Keep current enablement for compatibility but require provenance, explicit model/spend metadata, warnings, and quota-aware auto-pause before accepting external recurring jobs.

options.title: Defer To RFC Cluster
options.body: Leave current behavior unchanged while routing the work into the scheduling provenance, cost budget, and reason-aware cron guardrail RFCs.

recommendation.title: Default Disabled With Diff
recommendation.body: Externally or plugin-registered recurring agent-turn jobs start disabled until an operator reviews a doctor/update diff and enables them, with explicit model or safe model policy required.

likelyOwner.reason: The current cron/gateway/plugin scheduling paths and latest release evidence most directly point to recent work by vincentkoc, with steipete adjacent on model selection.
